assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: @TableTest appears twice in the code: validateRegistration and registrationPricing methods both use @TableTest(...)

assertions.text: Email validation and name-required error scenarios are present — at least one row for invalid email and one for missing name.
assertions.evidence: Null name row with error 'Name is required', Null email with 'Invalid email format', plus 'Email missing @' and 'Email missing domain' rows

assertions.text: Dietary requirements and/or accessibility needs use blank cells (null) when not provided — not 'N/A' or 'none'. These are genuinely optional and absent.
assertions.evidence: In validation table: 'Valid, no optional fields | Alice Smith | ... | | | true' - dietary and accessibility columns are blank

assertions.text: When testing pricing rules, irrelevant inputs (e.g. dietary requirements don't affect price) use value sets or representative values — not blanks (which mean null). Blanks are reserved for genuinely absent/null inputs.
assertions.evidence: Pricing table omits irrelevant dietary/accessibility columns entirely; description states 'null for all rows'

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Both tables have 'Scenario' as the first column header

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Result?', 'Price?')
assertions.evidence: Validation table has 'Accepted?' and 'Error?' columns; pricing table has 'Price?' column

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Name', 'Email', 'Registration date', 'Group size', 'Price?') — not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: All columns use business terms: Name, Email, Dietary req., Accessibility needs, Accepted?, Error?, Registration date, Group size, Price?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Early-bird single attendee', 'Missing name') — not outcomes ('Rejected', '20% off').
assertions.evidence: 'No discount' scenario names the outcome (no discount applied) rather than the conditions (after cutoff, single attendee) that produce it

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Both validateRegistration and registrationPricing methods contain only register() call and assertThat assertions; no control flow

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Both methods follow @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest in that order

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName('Registration validation') and @DisplayName('Registration pricing') with matching method names

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: Both @Description annotations use triple-quoted strings ("""...""")

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Two separate @TableTest methods: validateRegistration for input validation, registrationPricing for pricing rules

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: Validation table: 8 rows testing name/email/optional fields boundary cases. Pricing table: 6 rows testing discount thresholds and interactions

assertions.text: Input validation and pricing/discount calculation are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: validateRegistration method is distinct from registrationPricing method with no overlap in concerns

assertions.text: Validation @TableTest includes Dietary Requirements and Accessibility Needs columns, with rows showing both null (blank) and non-null values are accepted — not hardcoded as null in the method body.
assertions.evidence: Validation table row 1: blank optional fields accepted. Row 2: 'Vegan' | 'Wheelchair ramp' accepted. Both have Accepted? = true

assertions.text: Registration date uses descriptive values (e.g. 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff') with a @TypeConverter method converting to actual dates — not raw date literals like '2025-02-28'. Readability over precision.
assertions.evidence: Table uses 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff'. @TypeConverter maps to LocalDate.of(2025, 2, 28), (2025, 3, 1), (2025, 3, 15)

assertions.text: If registration dates are literal (e.g. '2025-02-28' instead of descriptive), the early-bird cutoff date appears as a separate policy column so the reader can see both dates and verify the comparison. Passes automatically if descriptive date values are used.
assertions.evidence: Descriptive date values are used, so automatic pass

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it does not include information that is already visible in the table columns or that can be derived from the table structure — such as fixed input values that could be columns, or restating the discount rules that the rows already demonstrate.
assertions.evidence: Pricing @Description states 'Early-bird (20% off) applies...' and 'Group discount (15% off) applies...' and 'higher discount wins' — all demonstrated by table rows

assertions.text: Output column is 'Discount?' (percentage or amount off) rather than 'Price?' — making verification simpler (discount is the rule's direct output; price requires knowing the base price). If 'Price?' is used instead, both 'Base price' and 'Price?' columns must be present so the reader can trace the calculation.
assertions.evidence: Pricing table uses 'Price?' column but lacks 'Base price' column; base price appears in @Description text, not as a table column

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method has a single, uniform assertion pattern applied to all rows — not different assertions per scenario. Validation checks one thing (e.g. error message or acceptance status); pricing checks one thing (e.g. discount or price). No if/switch in assertion logic.
assertions.evidence: validateRegistration: both assertions (isAccepted, getErrorMessage) applied uniformly to all rows. registrationPricing: both assertions (isAccepted, getPrice) applied uniformly

assertions.text: The optional-fields acceptance table includes an expectation/output column (e.g. 'Approved?', 'Result?', or 'Status?') asserting that each combination is accepted — not just varying inputs without any expected column.
assertions.evidence: Validation table rows 1-2 test optional fields with 'Accepted?' column; both null and non-null combinations have Accepted? = true

assertions.text: Scenario descriptions do not include specific field values that are already visible in the table or that serve as 'any valid value' placeholders. Stating 'name: John, email: john@example.com, registration date: 2025-04-01' in a description adds maintenance burden without value — it suffices to say 'valid values supplied' or describe the scenario condition. Applies to all tables.
assertions.evidence: No scenario names include specific values like 'name: John'; all names describe conditions or scenarios without field-level detail
